The operative relief suspends the eight-hour prohibition solely for construction and completion of surveying vessel PILOT; the quoted enabling proviso preserves a basic eight-hour wage rate and overtime of at least time and one-half. This is relief during construction, not an order proving that construction occurred or completed. No held completion fact or extinguishing provision establishes its first cessation. research_rationale: Full replica page 1 identifies EO 3522, Harding, July 27, 1921, amending paragraphs 40, 186 and 195 of the July 9, 1914 navigation rules. Paragraph 40 governs recurring vessel information and arrival reports with a prior-communication exception; 186 requires spark/smoke precautions and imposes damage liability; 195 requires registration/numbering or registration/certification and prohibits operation pending compliance. II supplies immediate commencement. These are continuing amended rules; an individual craft compliance event cannot terminate the general rule. Parent and subsequent provisions, first cessations and savings are not established. Frozen OCR corrupts parent year and paragraph identifiers. No whole-case submission.
savings_reason: Paragraph 186 expressly holds vessels liable for damage from neglect; no damage occurrence or outstanding liability is assumed. Paragraph 195 registration/certification may have consequences distinct from prospective rule operation. Parent and later text/savings are required to separate continuing duties, accrued liability and existing registrations. No finding that all consequences vanished.
